key_insight: A PDE-consistent neural-network closure trained inside the LES solver can learn turbulence–chemistry coupling in premixed jet flames and outperform a Smagorinsky baseline across Damköhler regimes.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical path to more accurate and stable LES models for turbulent combustion, improving both mean fields and resolved turbulence statistics without losing physical consistency.
method: Augmented eddy-viscosity closure built with deep neural networks
Solver-in-the-loop training using adjoint-based optimization and differentiable programming
Joint calibration with the LES solution to enforce consistency with the governing PDEs
evidence_signal: Compared with Smagorinsky, the best model reduced a posteriori LES primitive-variable errors by 25–50% and improved resolved Reynolds stress and scalar flux by more than 60%, while remaining stable on out-of-sample Damköhler numbers.
watch_item: Training and deployment rely on differentiable solver infrastructure and careful objective design, so stability and generalization may depend on how well the target regime is represented during calibration.
paper_title: Solver-in-the-loop training of deep learning closures for large-eddy simulation of turbulent premixed jet flames
